title: UPSC CSAT Paper II — Hard Simulation 4

rubric.reasoning_layers: At least two linked deductions, constraints or conditional checks in every non-trivial item.
rubric.distractor_quality: All four options are plausible, distinct and comparable in visible length and specificity.
rubric.time_pressure: Complete paper: 80 questions in 120 minutes; revision drill: 40 questions in 75 minutes.

rubric.verification: Every keyed answer is recomputed or independently constraint-checked before PDF generation.

questions.text: With reference to Passage 1, which one of the following best captures its central claim? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: That the use of evidence in welfare delivery should be left to spontaneous private action without accountable public oversight.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery is mainly technical and therefore has no significant distributive consequences.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery requires aligned incentives, evidence and local feedback rather than one universal prescription.
That the use of evidence in welfare delivery can be solved through one nationwide institutional reform under all conditions.
questions.solution: The passage links the issue to incentives, evidence and feedback; the alternatives are absolute or narrowly framed.

questions.text: Which one of the following is most directly inferable from Passage 1? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: A locally successful intervention will work identically elsewhere without any adaptation or review.
Measurement adds little when an intervention has a persuasive and desirable objective.
Administrative discretion is always harmful, even when evidence reveals local constraints.
An intervention may fail despite a desirable objective when its feedback loop remains weak.
questions.solution: The passage distinguishes a desirable objective from the quality of its feedback loop; it rejects universal claims.

questions.text: Which one of the following assumptions is necessary for the argument in Passage 1? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Every measurable outcome is morally decisive regardless of the chosen public objective.
Central rules are never useful, even when they protect minimum entitlements.
Institutional learning can improve policy without requiring perfect foresight at the outset.
Local actors always possess complete information before implementation begins.
questions.solution: The argument depends on learning through feedback; it does not require perfect information or reject all central rules.

questions.text: If r is the remainder when 6^21 + 7^19 is divided by 11, what is r? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Compute powers modulo 11; cyclic reduction gives remainder 3.

questions.text: How many integers from 2 through 99, inclusive, are divisible by 7 or 15, but not by both? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Count multiples of 7 and 15, then remove twice the common multiples: the exclusive count is 20.

questions.text: Solution A contains 18% solute and solution B contains 23% solute. If A and B are mixed in the volume ratio 7:1, what is the resulting concentration? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Use a weighted average: (7×18+23)/(7+1) = 18.62%.

questions.text: Three independent teams complete a task in 19, 26 and 42 days respectively. Working together at constant rates, how many days are required? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/19+1/26+1/42; reciprocal = 8.70 days.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row. C is third from the left; A is left of D; B and F are non-adjacent; G is not at an end. Which person cannot occupy fifth position? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
options: B
A
C
D
questions.solution: Enumerating all valid arrangements gives possible fifth-position occupants ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']; C never appears there.

questions.text: Six candidates P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked first to sixth. P is above R, R above U, S above R, Q below S, and T is not first. Which candidate cannot be third? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: R
Q
U
P
questions.solution: Testing all rankings gives possible third-place candidates ['P', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'T']; U violates the partial-order constraints in every valid ranking.

questions.solution: Y contains X plus Y-only members: 7+7 = 14.

questions.text: A field worker moves 5 km east and then 7 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point, ignoring the path taken? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Displacement = sqrt(5²+7²) = 8.60 km.

questions.text: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. P is the daughter of Q. Relative to P, what is M? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: P's paternal cousin
P's maternal aunt
P's grandmother
P's paternal aunt
questions.solution: N is P's father; M is N's sister, so M is P's paternal aunt.

questions.text: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Who is guilty? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: No one
A only
B only
C only
questions.solution: Assume exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Testing A, B and C in turn leaves only B guilty: A and C are then false, while B is true.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. A measurement conflicts with credible user reports before a sanction is proposed. What should precede action? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: Treat the instrument as conclusive because numerical readings are always objective.
Suspend the entire programme immediately without checking either source of information.
Triangulate the reading, maintenance record and a time-bound sample of affected users.
Treat oral reports as conclusive because lived experience cannot contain measurement error.
questions.solution: Triangulation tests measurement and lived experience before a consequential administrative action.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. A public message must announce an uncertain hazard. Which communication is most responsible? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: Offer absolute reassurance so that uncertainty does not increase public anxiety.
State known facts, uncertainty, protective action and the timing of the next update.
Release raw technical figures without an instruction that people can follow.
Wait until every uncertainty disappears before communicating with the affected public.
questions.solution: Responsible risk communication is candid about uncertainty while giving a clear time-bound action.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. Scarce services must be allocated between a larger population and a higher untreated-need rate. What rule is soundest? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Rotate resources randomly so that no indicator receives an explicit priority.
Use a transparent composite rule weighting scale, severity and access barriers.
Use population alone because scale is the only indicator that can be compared.
Use untreated-need rate alone because severity should always override the population base.
questions.solution: A transparent composite rule recognises scale and severity while making trade-offs reviewable.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. questions.solution: The indicator must track intended outcomes and be protected against gaming through verification.

questions.solution: Complaint counts need accessibility and independent-feedback checks before they can indicate improvement.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. questions.solution: A documented risk and change-control assessment protects safety without making procedure an empty ritual.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. A beneficiary list contains duplicate names and some genuine exclusions. What is the right sequence? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Delete all duplicate-looking names first and accept the resulting list as final.
Deduplicate transparently, publish an appeal window and verify excluded claims.
Add every claimant immediately and leave verification to a later unrecorded exercise.
Freeze enrolment indefinitely because cleaning the list may create further disputes.
questions.solution: Transparent deduplication plus appeal and verification addresses both leakage and wrongful exclusion.

questions.text: In a small municipality, a file concerning street-vending permits is being reviewed by licensing staff; the available evidence includes permit and footfall records. Apply the published hardship criteria equally and document any exceptional decision.
Ask the leader to obtain informal consent from staff before changing the record.

questions.solution: Equal application of a published rule protects fairness while allowing genuinely defined hardship relief.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A new digital process excludes some intended users. What should the officer do first? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
options: Ask users to arrange private help while leaving the official process unchanged.
Retain the process, add assisted access and an auditable fallback, then review evidence.
Require universal digital use so that one procedure applies to every applicant.
Cancel the process and restore the former manual arrangement for every applicant.
questions.solution: The response preserves useful innovation while removing exclusion through assisted access, fallback and review.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. Create a shared evidence set, record assumptions and commission a rapid joint verification.
Choose the record from the agency with the larger budget and proceed immediately.
questions.solution: A shared evidence base and explicit assumptions address disagreement without arbitrary choice or paralysis.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. Count publicity material and attendance figures because visibility indicates institutional effort.
questions.solution: Outcome-by-issue plus verified follow-up distinguishes visible activity from effective service delivery.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A fund can support a visible ceremony or a tested low-cost intervention. Which decision is stronger? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Divide funds equally even if neither activity then has enough resources to operate.
Choose the visible event because all stakeholders can observe its immediate completion.
Choose neither option until the underlying problem disappears without further intervention.
Choose the tested intervention, publish the baseline and specify a review point.
questions.solution: The evidence-supported intervention creates an accountable learning loop and a reviewable use of funds.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A lowest bid has a minor clerical error but no evidence of material advantage. What is fairest? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: Apply the published correction rule consistently and record the reasons for the decision.
Invite the bidder to alter unrelated parts of the submission before evaluation continues.
Ignore the error silently so that the procurement record remains uncomplicated.
Reject the bid automatically because any clerical error establishes bad faith.
questions.solution: Consistent use of a pre-published rule protects equal treatment, transparency and auditability.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A measurement conflicts with credible user reports before a sanction is proposed. What should precede action? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: Triangulate the reading, maintenance record and a time-bound sample of affected users.
Treat the instrument as conclusive because numerical readings are always objective.
Treat oral reports as conclusive because lived experience cannot contain measurement error.
Suspend the entire programme immediately without checking either source of information.
questions.solution: Triangulation tests measurement and lived experience before a consequential administrative action.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A public message must announce an uncertain hazard. Which communication is most responsible? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: State known facts, uncertainty, protective action and the timing of the next update.
Wait until every uncertainty disappears before communicating with the affected public.
Release raw technical figures without an instruction that people can follow.
Offer absolute reassurance so that uncertainty does not increase public anxiety.
questions.solution: Responsible risk communication is candid about uncertainty while giving a clear time-bound action.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Use population alone because scale is the only indicator that can be compared.
Rotate resources randomly so that no indicator receives an explicit priority.
Use a transparent composite rule weighting scale, severity and access barriers.
Use untreated-need rate alone because severity should always override the population base.
questions.solution: A transparent composite rule recognises scale and severity while making trade-offs reviewable.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A performance target encourages staff to close cases without resolving them. What correction is best? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
options: Punish the last staff member who closed a case without changing the target design.
Pair closure with verified resolution and sample audits, then revise the incentive.
Abolish measurement entirely because every indicator creates some risk of gaming.
Raise the target further so that staff complete cases at a faster average rate.
questions.solution: The indicator must track intended outcomes and be protected against gaming through verification.

questions.text: In an industrial cluster, a file concerning worker-safety inspections is being reviewed by factory inspectors; the available evidence includes incident and audit reports. A vocal association claims to represent everyone, but consultation attendance is narrow. What should follow? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.

Record its view and widen outreach through accessible channels before concluding.
Decide only by the loudest vote among participants already present in the room.
Exclude the association from later consultations because its claim cannot be trusted.
questions.solution: The process respects the association's input without mistaking it for complete representation.
